Diese Seite auf Deutsch: xref:user/de/third-party/home-assistant.adoc[OpenEMS: Home-Assistant-Integration]

__As of: 2026-11-01 · OpenEMS version 2026.11.0-SNAPSHOT (development version, branch develop)__

This page describes the Home Assistant integration **“Fenecon FEMS & OpenEMS”** (ha_openems, version 1.8.0, installation via HACS, at least Home Assistant 2026.8.0). It is a third-party project and **not** part of OpenEMS or FENECON. It is based on the source code of the integration and the OpenEMS source code; it has not been tried out here.

The page xref:user/third-party/overview.adoc[Third-party systems on OpenEMS] gives a comparison with evcc and openWB.

In short: like the web interface, the integration connects to the system via the xref:user/external-interfaces/websocket.adoc[websocket], turns components into devices and values (“channels”) into entities in Home Assistant, receives the values live and can change **settings**. It only sets **control values** (e.g. “charge the storage with 2 kW now”) via an additional service that uses the xref:user/external-interfaces/rest-control.adoc[REST interface].

[#sec-setting-up-the-connection]
== Setting up the connection

When adding the integration, you specify the address, user name and password. For a local system, the user name is arbitrary (the instructions mention “x”); what matters is the password, which determines the role (see xref:user/external-interfaces/websocket.adoc#sec-functions-and-user-roles[User roles]). The connection type is selected under “More options”:

[cols="3*",options="header"]
|===
| Connection type
| Address
| Remote station

| Direct connection to the system (default)
| ws://system:8085/
| Websocket interface of the Edge (Controller.Api.Websocket)
| FEMS local
| ws://system:80/websocket
| Web interface of the FEMS, which forwards to the websocket
| OpenEMS local
| ws://host:8082/
| your own OpenEMS backend (port 8082 is its default for the interface)
| FENECON online monitoring
| wss://portal.fenecon.de/…
| FENECON backend via the internet
| Custom address
| free
| e.g. behind a proxy
|===

For all local types, the connection is **unencrypted** (ws, not wss). Password and data therefore pass through the home network in plain text. Home Assistant stores the credentials in its own configuration.

For a backend with several systems, the integration queries the list of systems (20 at most) and creates one entry per system.

[#sec-how-communication-works]
== How communication works

The integration uses the same commands as the web interface (see xref:user/external-interfaces/websocket.adoc#sec-what-happens-after-opening-the-web-interface[What happens after opening the web interface]). All requests to the system are wrapped in an “edgeRpc” envelope with the system ID. This also works with the direct connection because the Edge also understands this envelope.

[#sec-during-setup]
=== During setup

. Open the connection and log in with user name and password. The integration logs in again with the password for each connection; a login token is not used.
. Read the configuration of the system: which components exist.
. Query the list of channels (with type, unit, read/write access) for **each** component individually. With 20 to 50 components, this is the same number of requests.
. Read the host name of the system and the names (aliases) of the components once via a second, short connection. The device names are created from this.
. Save the result of steps 2 to 4 in the entry of the integration in Home Assistant.
. Create a device for each component and an entity for each channel.

[#sec-at-every-start-of-home-assistant]
=== At every start of Home Assistant

. Open the connection and log in as above.
. The components, channels and names are **not** read anew from the system. The integration uses the list saved during setup or the last reload.
. Create devices and entities from this list; existing ones are reused.

[#sec-when-reloading]
=== When reloading

Steps 2 to 5 of setup run again if

* you “reload” or reconfigure the entry in Home Assistant, or
* the saved list is empty.

The same applies if the system could not be reached when Home Assistant started. Home Assistant then only repeats the attempt when it has fully started up. If the connection succeeds, the integration reads the list anew as when reloading.

The list is not read anew in the event of a connection failure with reconnection (see below) and when changing the options, i.e. when activating or deactivating components.

[#sec-during-operation]
=== During operation

. The integration registers the system and the list of **activated** entities (“subscribe”). Only activated entities are subscribed to; all others cost nothing during operation.
. The system sends the values of these channels about **every second**.
. If entities are activated or deactivated, the integration adjusts the subscription within about 5 seconds.
. Optionally (“Limit data updates”), it only passes on the values to Home Assistant every N seconds. This reduces the amount of data in the Home Assistant database; the system still sends every second.

[#sec-connection-failure]
=== Connection failure

* If no values arrive for **60 seconds**, the connection is considered lost.
* All entities then become “unavailable”.
* The integration tries to re-establish the connection every 10 seconds, logs in again and subscribes again.

[#sec-what-is-not-transferred]
=== What is not transferred

* **No history from the system.** The integration does not read any stored histories (see xref:user/data/history-rrd4j.adoc[History]). Home Assistant builds its own history from the live values. If Home Assistant is not running, a gap arises there even though the system continues to record.
* **Configuration changes in the system** (new component, new app) are not adopted automatically. To do this, you must “reload” the entry in Home Assistant. According to the code, the message from the system about a changed configuration is currently not evaluated.

[#sec-what-appears-in-home-assistant]
== What appears in Home Assistant

[cols="2*",options="header"]
|===
| OpenEMS
| Home Assistant

| System
| Entry of the integration (name from the host name)
| Component (e.g. ess0, meter0, ctrlEvcs0)
| Device
| Measured value (e.g. power, state of charge)
| Sensor
| Yes/no value (e.g. warnings)
| Binary sensor
| Yes/no setting
| Switch
| Setting with selection list
| Select
| Setting with number
| Number (only for stored settings, see below)
| Setting with time
| Time (only for stored settings)
| System update of the system
| Update entity
|===

**Default:** After setup, only some components and only a few channels within them are active, including the total values (`+_sum+`: consumption, production, grid, storage), state of charge and energy meter of the storage, power of meters and PV inverters, the emergency reserve, the charge point settings, grid-optimized charge, battery extension, § 14a and the release for charging from the grid. Further components can be added in the options of the integration, further entities activated in the entity list. The instructions advise against activating several hundred channels at the same time.

The energy meters from `+_sum+` (grid purchase, feed-in, production, storage charge and discharge, see xref:user/basics/energy-flows.adoc[Energy flows]) are suitable for the Home Assistant **energy dashboard**.

[#sec-additional-calculated-values]
=== Additional calculated values

For batteries, the integration itself calculates the **voltage difference** between the highest and lowest cell, for the entire battery and per module. OpenEMS does not supply these values directly; they are created from the cell voltages (see xref:user/systems/fenecon-home-battery.adoc[FENECON Home battery]). For this, the cell voltage channels must be activated.

[#sec-ready-made-cards]
=== Ready-made cards

The integration comes with templates for dashboard cards: charge point, grid-optimized charge, emergency reserve, heating element and a battery diagnostics dashboard. They need additional card extensions from HACS.

[#sec-what-can-be-controlled]
== What can be controlled

The integration has three write routes. They differ fundamentally:

[cols="5*",options="header"]
|===
| Route
| What
| How
| Duration
| Required role

| Changing a setting
| Switch, select, number, time; action “Update component configuration”
| updateComponentConfig via the websocket
| **permanent**, is stored
| Owner
| Setting a control value
| Action “REST write sensor” on a sensor
| POST to the REST interface of the system
| temporary, only as long as repeated
| according to the REST page Owner; REST write app required
| System update
| Update entity “Install”
| Call to `+_host+` via the websocket
| –
| Owner
|===

The integration does not use the websocket command for setting control values (setChannelValue); in OpenEMS it is reserved for the Admin.

[#sec-settings]
=== Settings

Each setting of a component (channels starting with “_Property”) becomes an entity:

* **Yes/no settings** always become switches, for **every** component. This also includes “enabled” (`+_PropertyEnabled+`), which can be used to switch off a component completely. These switches are deactivated by default but available.
* **Selection lists** are created if the system supplies the options or the integration knows them, e.g. charging mode and priority at the charge point, mode of grid-optimized charge, mode of the heating element, power distribution strategy (`+_power+`), risk level of the energy optimizer.
* **Numbers** only for settings for which the integration has stored limits: emergency reserve (percent), energy limit and minimum power values at the charge point, energy limit at the EVSE charge point, minimum running time of the heating element.
* **Times**: target time of grid-optimized charge, end time of the heating element.

With the action **“Update component configuration”** (“update_component_config”), several settings of a component can be changed in **one** request. The integration only checks whether a value is a number, a switch value, a time or a valid selection; it does not check the minimum and maximum values of numbers. For charge points (ctrlEvcs), the integration sends both settings together when changing the charging mode and when switching on “Charging enabled”.

**Important – memory wear:** Every change to a setting is **stored permanently** in the system and restarts the function concerned. Automations that switch settings frequently (for example every minute) can wear out the flash memory of the system in the long term. See xref:user/external-interfaces/websocket.adoc#sec-note-do-not-write-the-configuration-frequently[Note: Do not write the configuration frequently]. Therefore only write settings in automations rarely and only when there is a real change.

[#sec-control-values-via-rest]
=== Control values via REST

For ongoing control, e.g. specifying a storage power or switching a relay, there is the action **“REST write sensor”** (or “REST write binary sensor” for binary sensors). It only works if the app or component **“REST/JSON API read/write access”** (Controller.Api.Rest.ReadWrite) is set up in the system; the integration recognizes this during setup.

* The integration sends the value via HTTP to `+/rest/channel/component/channel+` of the system, with the same credentials as for the websocket (see xref:user/external-interfaces/rest-control.adoc#sec-setting-a-control-value[Setting a control value]).
* Because the system discards a control value after the Api-Timeout (default 60 seconds), the integration **repeats** the value every 30 seconds by default. “Timeout” can be used to specify for how long; 0 means “until the next call for this entity”. “Update cycle 0” only sends once.
* A control value is only held in RAM; this is the right route for frequent changes.
* You **cannot** see in Home Assistant whether the value has arrived: the system does not report written control values back. Only errors (e.g. wrong password, “is not a Write Channel”) appear in the Home Assistant log.
* The integration always forms the REST address as an unencrypted address (http) from the host name of the websocket address and the port set in the REST app (default 8084). There is no address you can specify yourself for this. If the system is behind a proxy that only forwards the websocket under this host name and not the REST port, the integration cannot reach the REST app. This route does not exist with FENECON online monitoring.

[#sec-system-update]
=== System update

The update entity queries the update status of the system every 12 hours and can start an update. This requires the Owner role and only works where the system itself offers a system update.

[#sec-limits]
== Limits

[cols="2*",options="header"]
|===
| Limit
| Consequence

| Third-party project, not from the manufacturer
| Changes to OpenEMS or FEMS can affect the integration at any time. According to the instructions, only a FENECON Home 10 with a few additional devices has been tested.
| Guest role
| Read only. Switches, selections etc. appear, but changing them fails.
| Settings are stored permanently
| Frequent switching wears out the memory of the system; use REST control values for ongoing control.
| Control values only via REST
| REST write app required, no feedback in Home Assistant, value must be repeated.
| Dangerous switches available
| E.g. “enabled” of each component. Anyone who activates such entities can switch off storage, meters or protective functions.
| No history from the system
| Gaps in Home Assistant when it is not running.
| Configuration is not automatically updated
| “Reload” after changes to the system.
| Unencrypted connection in the home network
| Do not expose port 8085 or 8084 to the internet.
| Many entities
| Load and data volume in Home Assistant; subscription only for activated entities.
| Meter readings after restart of the system
| According to the code of the integration, the system sometimes reports meter readings that are too low shortly after a restart. The option “Ignore decreasing if total increasing” discards such values so that the statistics in Home Assistant do not jump.
| Several systems on one backend
| At most 20 are listed.
| System limits continue to apply
| Emergency reserve, battery and grid limits restrict specifications; a control value is not always implemented in full.
|===

[#sec-typical-questions]
== Typical questions

**Can I have the storage charged or discharged from Home Assistant?**

Yes, via the action “REST write sensor” on the entity for the setpoint power of the storage, e.g. `+ess0/SetActivePowerEquals+` (negative = charge). The prerequisite is the REST write app. The entity must be activated in Home Assistant for this. The integration repeats the value until the timeout expires or a new call arrives.

**Why does nothing change in Home Assistant after I have written a REST value?**

The control value itself is not reported back. Only the effect can be seen, e.g. in the actual storage power.

**I set up a new app in the system, but it is missing in Home Assistant.**

Reload the entry of the integration and add the new component in the options.

**The system log says “Unable to read value for Channel [meter1/ActivePower]” every second even though the meter is deactivated.**

The message does not come from the meter, but from the websocket interface: Home Assistant queries values of a component that is deactivated in the system. The integration also offers deactivated components, but the system does not supply any values for them and writes this warning in every cycle. Remedy: deselect the component in the options of the integration or deactivate its entities in Home Assistant. If the component is no longer needed in the system at all, you can also delete it there.

**May I adjust the emergency reserve daily via automation?**

Occasionally yes. Each change is stored permanently; several times a day is still not critical, every minute is (see xref:user/external-interfaces/websocket.adoc#sec-note-do-not-write-the-configuration-frequently[Note]).

**Websocket or REST for Home Assistant?**

The integration uses both: the websocket for live values and settings, REST only for control values. For a comparison, see xref:user/external-interfaces/websocket.adoc#sec-websocket-or-rest[Websocket or REST?].
